requirements.title: EXTERNAL statements specify the EXTERNAL attribute for listed names
requirements.definition: An EXTERNAL statement specifies the EXTERNAL attribute for each name in its external-name-list.

pending.external-statement-specifies-attribute: PENDING positive source plan: a main program declares EXTERNAL :: f and passes f as an actual procedure to an explicit-interface caller; exact callback result f(5)==16 is observed with result sentinel -16, while procedure-call semantics remain with 15.5.
pending.external-name-list-each-name: PENDING source plan: EXTERNAL :: f, g declares two external functions used as actual procedures in separate exact callbacks returning 16 and 27 from sentinels -16 and -27.
pending.external-attribute-dependency: PENDING source-control plan maps the attribute effect to 8.5.9 and keeps missing-attribute restrictions under their canonical owners rather than this statement overview.
pending.external-intrinsic-name-shadowing: PENDING positive intrinsic-shadowing plan: compile a separate external procedure REAL FUNCTION ABS(X) with REAL, INTENT(IN) :: X and result 42.0 + X, and in the caller declare REAL, EXTERNAL :: ABS before evaluating ABS(-1.0); expect exact 41.0 from a result variable initialized to sentinel -41.0, proving that the 15.4.3.5 EXTERNAL statement supplies the 8.5.9 EXTERNAL attribute and the reference resolves to the external procedure rather than the standard generic intrinsic ABS. Companion control in a separate caller omits EXTERNAL and any explicit interface for ABS, evaluates ABS(-1.0), and expects exact 1.0 from the intrinsic; cite 16.7 for ABS as a standard generic intrinsic and 16.9.2 p5 for exact integer and real absolute-value results. Do not add an INTRINSIC statement in the EXTERNAL case, because 8.5.9 C842 forbids both attributes for the same entity. 19.5.1.4 p2 is relevant only for host-associated shadowing: an external-procedure name given EXTERNAL in a scoping unit is a global identifier that makes a same-named host entity inaccessible.

requirements.oracle: Pending plans are source-derived and discriminate the named EXTERNAL-statement property from neighboring syntax, procedure characteristics, intrinsic semantics, or invocation rules. Runtime plans use distinct sentinels and compare only exact scalar values fixed by the registered source text; the intrinsic-shadowing plan distinguishes external ABS(-1.0)==41.0 from intrinsic ABS(-1.0)==1.0, with the intrinsic numeric control re-derived from 16.9.2 p5 before fixture binding.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Source registration only: no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim is created. Future fixtures must establish a non-default positive state before the observation; diagnostics require the numbered rule or syntax rule named by the facet and a conforming control differing only in the constrained feature. Notes and examples are not normative.
requirements.dependencies: Dependencies retained: 8.5.9 for the EXTERNAL attribute and C842 attribute conflict; 8.5.11 for INTRINSIC identity where explicitly used; 15.4.3.2/.3/.4 for interface and generic relationships; 15.5 for procedure invocation; 16.7 and 16.9.2 for ABS as a standard generic intrinsic and its exact integer and real absolute-value results; 19.5.1.4 p2 for host-associated global-identifier shadowing by EXTERNAL names where that premise is reached; processor conformance diagnostics in 4.2.

requirements.title: An EXTERNAL statement has optional double colon and a required external-name list
requirements.definition: The EXTERNAL statement syntax is EXTERNAL followed by an optional double colon and a nonempty external-name-list.

pending.external-with-double-colon: PENDING compile/positive-control: complete program with INTEGER, EXTERNAL :: f and an external integer function f; no invocation is needed for grammar admission, and a separate callback control observes f(5)==16.
pending.external-without-double-colon: PENDING compile/positive-control: same complete program using EXTERNAL f; all type, external function definition, and absence of duplicate attributes are unchanged.
pending.external-multiple-names: PENDING compile/positive-control: EXTERNAL :: f, g with two external integer functions and optional callback checks returning exact 16 and 27 from sentinels.
pending.external-required-name-list: PENDING diagnostic/control pair: EXTERNAL alone and EXTERNAL :: alone are repaired only by adding prior declared external name f; the program remains otherwise complete and conforming.
pending.external-single-colon-negative: PENDING diagnostic/control pair: EXTERNAL : f is repaired only by changing the separator to ::, with the same external function f and no attribute or type changes.
pending.external-list-separator-negative: PENDING diagnostic/control pair: EXTERNAL :: f g and EXTERNAL :: f, are repaired only by adding or removing the comma; both names remain valid external names in the corresponding positive control.

requirements.oracle: Grammar diagnostics are required for malformed R1511 forms, but no exact diagnostic text, code, or fatal exit status is prescribed. Positive controls isolate the syntax from procedure invocation.

requirements.title: An EXTERNAL statement naming block data confirms that block data program unit is part of the program
requirements.definition: The appearance of a block data program unit name in an EXTERNAL statement confirms that the block data program unit is part of the program.

pending.block-data-name-in-external: PENDING source-control plan: complete program contains EXTERNAL :: initblk and a separate BLOCK DATA initblk with a named COMMON block initialized to exact value 37; the source relation identifies initblk as a block data name rather than a procedure.
pending.block-data-program-membership-confirmed: PENDING build-composition plan: a future harness may link the block data program unit as a separate program unit and observe COMMON variable value 37 after initialization, but the source packet records only the membership confirmation.
pending.block-data-runtime-oracle-limited: PENDING limitation record: a single self-contained source file containing the BLOCK DATA unit already makes that unit part of the submitted program, so removing EXTERNAL is not a load-bearing mutation for this facet.

requirements.oracle: The portable core is a source/program-composition relation. A future executable plan must separate program-unit membership from ordinary presence of a BLOCK DATA unit in the same submitted source.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No portable single-source runtime oracle isolates the EXTERNAL statement's membership confirmation from the ordinary inclusion of a BLOCK DATA program unit already present in the source file. Linker retention policies and object-file selection are processor/build-system behavior, not a language result fixed by this paragraph.
